# parity-fuzz --mode tied baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode tied --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean. Covers `typeset -T` ties: both
# assignment directions, custom separators, empty fields, element assignment,
# the shell's own PATH/path pair, -U on a tie, and re-tying.
#
# Every divergence this mode found was a real port bug and was FIXED:
#
#   1. `typeset -U path; path=(/a /b /a)` left $PATH as `/a:/b:/a` while $path
#      was `/a /b` — the two halves of ONE tie disagreeing with each other. The
#      fusevm tie mirror joined the RAW values; c:Src/params.c:4066-4076
#      arrsetfn fixes the order —
#          if (pm->node.flags & PM_UNIQUE) uniqarray(x);
#          pm->u.arr = x;
#          if (pm->ename && x) arrfixenv(pm->ename, x);
#      — the dedupe happens BEFORE the scalar is published, so they cannot
#      drift apart. This is `typeset -U path`, the PATH-dedup idiom in
#      essentially every .zshrc.
#
#   2. `typeset -UT` tied the pair but dropped the -U entirely: the tie
#      attributes were masked to PM_EXPORTED|PM_READONLY where C hands BOTH
#      halves the full `on` (c:2989/3003). `on` has already had its type bits
#      stripped at c:2742-2744, so carrying it whole is safe.
#
#   3. The whole c:2903-2973 block was missing — the decision between erroring,
#      re-tying, and UPDATING an existing tie. The -T handler just installed a
#      fresh pair every time, so it silently accepted three cases C rejects and
#      lost every attribute the new command line did not restate:
#        - c:2903-2918 special tied pair (PATH/path): only an identical re-tie
#          is legal. `typeset -T PATH other` must fail with "PATH special
#          parameter can only be tied to special parameter path" — it was
#          silently UNTYING PATH — and `typeset -T PATH path ';'` must fail with
#          "cannot change the join character of special tied parameters".
#        - c:2930-2943 plain scalar already tied: re-tying it to a different
#          array must fail with "can't tie already tied scalar".
#        - c:2957-2973 already_tied: C does NOT rebuild. It runs typeset_single
#          on each half "if only to update the attributes of both, and of
#          course to set the new value if one is provided", then returns.
#          Applying on/off to the EXISTING entries is what lets an attribute the
#          command doesn't restate survive, so `typeset -UT TS ts; typeset -T TS
#          ts` keeps its uniqueness (and readonly likewise). typeset_single also
#          takes `joinchar`, so a re-tie restates the separator: `typeset -T TS
#          ts; typeset -T TS ts ,` must join on ',' while staying tied.
#
# Structural note, since it is what let all three live: the port of
# typeset_single EXISTS in builtin.rs but is DEAD CODE — nothing references it —
# while bin_typeset carries its own inline logic. That is the same
# faithful-port-shadowed-by-a-reimplementation shape behind the (D)/substnamedir
# bug. The already_tied attribute update is therefore applied directly in
# bin_typeset rather than routed through typeset_single; wiring that dead port
# back in is the real cleanup and would subsume it.
#
# This mode gated ties from the start but never once combined one with -U, which
# is how (1) and (2) survived a green gate. The -U arms print BOTH halves —
# checking only $TS or only ${#ts} cannot see a one-sided dedupe.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
